questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.4\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force 

$$
F(t)=(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t)-2)\,\text{N}
$$

is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.4{y}^{″}=-ky+(4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t)-2).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5k}{2}y=5(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t)-1).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=\frac{5k}{2}\,⟹\,k=\frac{2}{5}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=5(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t)-1)$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$ Since

$$
f(t)=5(2{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t)-1)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t),
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $3.$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{2}{5}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{2}{5}\cdot {3}^{2}=\frac{18}{5}\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

{y}^{″}+2ky=4{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{3}{2}t).

$$

$$

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)-\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $3.$ Therefore,
$\omega =3.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =3$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[9(D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-9(C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)]+9t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 9D\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-9C\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=-\frac{2}{3}$ and $D=0.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)-\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)-\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\frac{2}{3}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)$

Only solution II matches the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $2.$ Therefore,
$\omega =2.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =2$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[4(D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4(C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)]+4t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)) & =-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 4D\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)-4C\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & =-7\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{7}{4}$ and $D=0.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t+ϕ)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{7}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)$

Only solutions I and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".

A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $3.$ Therefore,
$\omega =3.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =3$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(6D-9Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-(6C+9Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)]+9t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 6D\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-6C\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{1}{2}$ and $D=-2.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)+\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Solutions I, II, and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".
